name: Uprights: Rugby Kicker
subtitle: Read the wind, strike true
shortDescription: A goal-kicking game with real flight: wind, altitude, nerves, six cups at six grounds and thirty challenges.
longDescription:
Rugby's goal kicker stands alone in front of the posts while the whole stadium falls quiet, and every ground has its own wind. Uprights is a rugby kicking game with a real physics model behind every kick. Stand over the ball in a 3D stadium, read the flags, set your aim and the strike on the ball, then hold and release. The ball flies through gusting wind, thin air or wet cold; it spins, curves and can clang off the post or the bar.

A kick asks you questions. Aim off into the wind and let it bring the ball back. Strike low for height or high for a flat drive. Swing smoothly up to 72 percent effort, or take a harder, riskier swing for distance. Nerves rise with the stakes and shake the ring and the aim line; a well-timed breath steadies you.

Six cups and thirty fixtures make a career at six grounds: a sea-level harbour, thin-air highveld, a damp fenland bowl, a gale-swept headland, a floodlit night match and a great covered arena. Each fixture is six kicks each against a rival kicker, with conversions, penalty goals and drop goals, the shot clock and a tie settled by extra kicks.

Thirty challenges cover wind school, touchline angles, long range, drop goals under a charge and pressure sets, with three kicks each and a star for every goal. A daily set of six kicks is the same for everyone. Practice lets you choose the spot, the ground, the wind and how much help the coach gives.
